newsitem.title: USA: Norfolk Southern suffers defeats in Conrail case.
newsitem.headline: Norfolk Southern suffers defeats in Conrail case.

text.p: Norfolk Southern Corp. suffered major setbacks Thursday on two fronts in its attempt to wrest Conrail Inc. from an intended merger with CSX Corp.

A U.S. District Court Judge in Philadelphia and the federal Surface Transportation Board each rejected separate requests by Norfolk Southern to invalidate a provision in the merger agreement by Conrail and CSX not to discuss a deal with a third party until 1999.

The ruling, if upheld on appeal, would mean Conrail could not consider Norfolk Southern's $10.3 billion bid for the Philadelphia-based railroad until 1999. The merger agreement between Conrail and CSX is worth about $9.1 billion at Thursday's stock trading prices.

The Philadelphia court also rejected a request by Norfolk Southern and a group of Conrail shareholders to order CSX to pay $110 cash for all of Conrail, rather than for only 40 percent as CSX has proposed. CSX intends to swap shares for the remaining 60 percent.

The Norfolk Southern request was based on a Pennsylvania anti-takeover law that requires a company or group that has acquired a stake of 20 percent or more in another firm to pay "fair value", or equivalent terms for all of the remaining shares.
In addition, the court refused Norfolk Souther's request to block a key Conrail shareholders meeting next week until a final legal decision could be reached on the "fair value" challenge.
A Norfolk Southern attorney immediately said the judge's rulings would be appealed.
A Conrail spokesman welcomed the decisions, saying they increased the prospects Conrail shareholders would vote in favour of the merger at the January 17 shareholders meeting.

Norfolk, Va.-based Norfolk Southern is pursuing a $115-per-share, $10.3 billion bid for Conrail, which has agreed to merge with Richmond, Va.-based CSX in a cash-and-stock deal worth about $101-per-share, or $9.1 billion.
In late trading on the New York Stock Exchange, Conrail stock was up 50 cents at $99.625, CSX was up $1.25 at $43.125, and Norfolk Southern was up $1.75 at $88.875.
